long_biography.plain_text:
When his father and uncle bought the Telegraph titles in 2004, Aidan Barclay became the newspaper group's executive chairman and the family's most visible business representative. He concentrated on budgets, strategy and digital expansion rather than editorial work, overseeing the titles' move to new London offices and a return to profit.

Barclay had previously managed Ellerman's property interests and chaired the family's Scottish newspapers and the Ritz hotel. Colleagues described a cautious operator who focused on targets, accounts and margins while leaving front-of-house traditions intact. That approach placed him at the centre of a private portfolio spanning media, retail, hotels and property.
